unnumbered_extensions.scope: Actual nearest finite affine grid, continuous primitive uniform law, fixed grid/scales; arbitrary SFinite measurable history with explicit joint integrability/L2. Actual Gram-derived projected gaps and noise-cross to bias-cross/event bounds. Fixed-alpha a.e. inverse qualification for the two concrete matrices. No dynamic range refitting, no whole-network harmlessness. Gap and gap-bound strengths are fixed. Energy and cross identities may use measurable upstream-history strength, but cannot observe the current fresh dither.

Actual continuous causal quantizer, fixed-coefficient triangular inverse, covariance and Frobenius energy, matched-Gram finite overload. Measurable random-upstream parameters preserve joint standardized innovation law; random physical-scale noise is not independent of upstream. No arbitrary random-parameter global energy/tower wrapper, no software GPTQ equivalence, no automatic LDL construction, no general block lattice. The teacher-loss identity is a single-row result with an explicit projection inner-product premise; it is not a fully assembled general multirow/random-history QEP loss theorem.

Deterministic pathwise scalar/matrix composite bounds, envelopes and legal neighborhoods for continuous perturbation paths of fixed finite depth. The existence radius may depend on the fixed strength and path; second-order constants are uniform only under a shared envelope. These are supporting extensions, not finite-probability moment theorems or newly numbered manuscript claims.
Earlier finite-support row-space/conditional-moment variants, actual row-space or equal-width inverse conditions retained. The stronger current linear result is mapped to its separate X1 modules.

Specific finite sign-law schedule comparison and U-squared counterexample. Not a continuous uniform-dither counterexample for U. Previously supplied continuous-dither counterexamples to mean-square ordering of the two schemes’ own-trajectory U bounds remain paper-only and are not Lean claims in this package.
Deterministic stability/margin algebra with explicit error bounds. Not a probabilistic certificate for trained networks.
New notes after Proposition 13 in Section 5: weighted positive-semidefinite contraction characterization and Frobenius commutator identities. Paper-level only; not formalized.
